rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin; a box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]
rules.floor: the yard is built round the old picture: a place on its lawn keeps its screen place. A frog place q: the ground point under (q.x + 16, q.y + 25), new q = old q. A person's place (x, y): the ground point under (x, y - 1), new (x, y) = old. So every ground position of patio.js, its stories and its pairs keeps its numbers, but for the few in moves; the sheet names each one (spots, remap, code, moves) with its world point
rules.relative: what the old code draws or moves relative to a person, the frog or a point (what they carry, the flower in Carmen's hair, the fireflies "with" someone, the bubbles, the ball at p.x + 12) keeps its offsets
rules.sky: screen-space effects keep their old numbers: the stars of the happy endings (final9, final10, final11), the heart (heartAt), the bird's loop (aveloop) and its flights, the fireflies' way out (stake: 226, 58)
rules.view: one view, zoom 1: the 196 x 216 window from x0 22, the old wide one
rules.pair: a review or level picture is pictures[word.side] (level: level[...].picture): zoom 1 = the 196 x 104 window crop; zoom 2 = the 98 x 52 crop shown nearest-neighbour at 2 x 2. The old rectangles (remap cam and crop) say which pictures they were

layout.what: the yard built as La sala is: two walls on the world's axes, seen at the engine's 30 degrees (shadows to screen right), coming together in a far corner over the middle of the picture, the lawn running off the picture's sides and bottom. On the LEFT the back of the house: its back wall on x = -1.904392167527876 (it faces +x, in shade, teal siding as El frente's side wall), from its far corner (a white corner board, screen x 76) down off the picture's left edge; in it the back door in its white frame on a stone step (screen x 34 to 69); over it a hip roof of red tiles, the hip over the far corner. On the FAR RIGHT the wooden fence on y = -1.604392167527876 (it faces +y, lit), from the far corner off the picture's right edge, posts with caps along it; in it, near the corner, the cream garden gate between two taller posts (screen x 115 to 163); right of the gate the flamboyán, its trunk a little in front of the fence, its crown where the old one was, the nest on a branch at its left. The lawn before them, the two beds of earth at the old ellipses. The house stops 2 units short of the corner: between its far corner and the fence's first post the yard opens on a field and low hills (the horizon at row 84), where the sun goes down. The gate opens into the yard: its leaf swung on its left post, its face seen; through the empty opening a path of trodden earth goes out over the field and winds up the hill behind. Through the open door a dark room (no story lights it): abuela stands in the doorway, on its threshold. The lawn is the yard's own green, calm (two neighbouring tones), no blooms in its grass round the beds, the crate and the ball; the beds are turned earth in lumps, a hole for each flower

behind.what: the sky is the set's (baked per hour); what moves or twinkles in it is the sprite layer's, drawn behind the set: the sun (sol(), its rays turning with F, sinking with W.soly), the moon (luna()) and the stars (ESTRELLAS, twinkling). Each is drawn first in the sprite layer, then the set's own pixels are drawn again inside its box wherever the set has drawn anything (bakedZ > -1e8, and the leaves of that frame): the sky objects are farther than everything (depth -1e9, SetOverSprites). The hills are the set's, at depth -10000000 (farther than any of the set's things, nearer than the sky objects). So the sun goes down behind the field and the hills in the gap between the house and the fence, and the house hides the stars at 40, 46 (as the old picture did), 60, 18 and 72, 64
